title: Sons Of Thunder
subject: Criminal Law & Procedure
stem:
Question ID: 14723_sons_of_thunder
Transformed from: 14723

Peter, John, and Barnabas were teenagers in a rowdy neighborhood crew that jokingly called itself the “Sons of Thunder” after a church Bible-trivia night. While they were driving home from a Christian-school dance late one evening, their car collided with a car driven by Ruth, an elderly woman.

After an argument, Peter attacked Ruth with his fists and beat her to death. John and Barnabas watched. When they saw Ruth fall to the ground, they urged Peter to run away. Peter was later arrested and tried for manslaughter, but the jury could not reach a verdict.

If John and Barnabas are later tried as accomplices to manslaughter, they should be:
call: If John and Barnabas are later tried as accomplices to manslaughter, they should be:

choices.A: Acquitted, because Peter was not convicted of the offense.
choices.B: Acquitted, because they did not assist or encourage Peter to commit the crime.
choices.C: Convicted, because they urged Peter to run away.
choices.D: Convicted, because they made no effort to intervene.

rightExplanation:
B is correct.

Gold Key: Accomplice liability requires aid, encouragement, counsel, command, inducement, procurement, or other assistance in the commission of the offense, plus the intent to facilitate that offense. Mere presence is not enough.

Silver Key: Lock the call to “accomplices to manslaughter.” Then split the facts by timing: help during the crime can matter; help after the fall / after the beating points to a different frame.

John and Barnabas watched the attack. The only affirmative words they gave came after Ruth fell, when they urged Peter to run. That does not assist or encourage the manslaughter itself. The responsive answer is therefore acquittal on the accomplice-to-manslaughter charge.

wrongExplanations.A: Peter’s lack of conviction does not by itself acquit John and Barnabas. Gold Key: Under the modern rule, an accomplice can be convicted even if the principal has not been convicted. A hung jury for Peter is not a shield for the companions.
wrongExplanations.C: This is the dominant trap. John and Barnabas did urge Peter to run, but that happened after Ruth fell. Silver Key: The call asks about accomplices to manslaughter, not whether they helped Peter escape afterward. Help after the crime points to an after-the-fact frame, not aiding the commission of the manslaughter.
wrongExplanations.D: Failure to intervene is not the same as assisting or encouraging the crime. Gold Key: Mere presence, silence, or failure to rescue does not create accomplice liability unless the person has a legal duty and acts with the required assisting intent.

c3.label: CUT
c3.text:
* A: Cut only with anchor. It reverses the modern principal-conviction rule.
* D: Cut with anchor. It invents liability from nonintervention / moral blame.

c3.label: CLASH
c3.text:
* B and C fight on timing and target.
* B: no aid or encouragement of the manslaughter.
* C: later urging Peter to run.
* Splitting fact: the urging came when Ruth fell, not before or during the attack.

c3.label: CALL
c3.text:
* Gold Key resolves the residue: after-the-fact help is not aiding the commission of manslaughter.
* Residual answer: B.

studentScript: Call: accomplices to manslaughter. Facts: they watched; only urged flight after Ruth fell; Peter was not convicted. A needs principal-conviction rule, cut by Gold Key. C is after-the-fact timing, not the manslaughter. D is moral duty, not legal aid. B remains.

A.signal: The answer makes acquittal depend on Peter's nonconviction. That dependency is not visible without the Gold Key.
A.lawyer: Modern accomplice liability does not require the principal's prior conviction; a principal's acquittal or nonconviction does not automatically bar aider-and-abettor liability.

B.signal: It answers the exact call: no aid or encouragement of Peter's commission of manslaughter.
B.lawyer: Accomplice liability requires affirmative assistance or encouragement in the commission of the offense with the required facilitating intent.

C.signal: The fact is true, but it points after the fall. The call asks about accomplices to the manslaughter.
C.lawyer: Post-offense assistance may fit accessory-after-the-fact framing, but it is not aiding the commission of the manslaughter.

D.signal: The answer turns failure to intervene into legal assistance. That requires the Gold Key.
D.lawyer: Mere presence and failure to intervene are generally insufficient for accomplice liability absent a duty plus intentional assistance.

goldKeys.statement: Accomplice liability requires intentional aid, encouragement, counsel, command, inducement, procurement, or assistance in the commission of the charged crime. Mere presence is not enough.
goldKeys.trigger: The accused watched the crime but did not help or encourage it before or during commission.
goldKeys.unlocks: B over D; the no-assistance residual
goldKeys.authority: 18 U.S.C. § 2; Rosemond v. United States, 572 U.S. 65 (2014)

goldKeys.statement: Help after the crime is complete may be accessory-after-the-fact conduct; it is not aid to the commission of the underlying crime.
goldKeys.trigger: The only assistance is urging flight after the victim falls.

goldKeys.statement: Modern accomplice liability does not require the principal to be convicted first.
goldKeys.trigger: The answer says the companion is acquitted because the principal was not convicted.

silverKeys.statement: When one answer says no aid and another points to flight help, lock the call to the charged crime and split the facts by timing: before/during the crime versus after the crime.
silverKeys.trigger: The only words of encouragement occur after the victim falls.

remediation.title: Accomplice timing: commission aid versus after-fact help
remediation.signal: The answer points to help escaping after the injury.
remediation.studentMove: Ask whether the help assisted the charged crime itself.
remediation.tinyRule: Accomplice to the crime requires aid or encouragement of the crime; after-the-fact help is a different lane.
remediation.trap: Treating any bad help as accomplice liability.
